title: A bored teenager can place 10 fake cash orders in 0.3 seconds with throwaway emails and nonsense phone numbers, and every one lands on the kitchen looking real
steps: Script a loop of 10 POSTs to /public/shops/mama-ades-kitchen/orders
Each with a random throwaway email and a junk phone ('call me', 'no', 'x', '0', '1')
fulfilmentType COLLECTION, one real product id, no auth, no browser
expected: Something slows a burst of guest orders down: a per-email / per-phone / per-device cap, email verification before the kitchen sees it, a captcha, or a hold queue
actual: All 10 returned 201 PENDING in 311 ms total. No verification, no captcha, no per-identity cap. They appear in the vendor's Orders list indistinguishable from real orders.
realWorldImpact: A small vendor prepping to a cash-on-collection screen cooks food for orders nobody collects. One teenager with a for-loop can bury a real Friday rush under junk and burn an evening of ingredients and prep time. The only cost to the attacker is typing.

title: The public rate limiter is defeated by sending a different X-Forwarded-For header each time
steps: GET /public/shops/mama-ades-kitchen/config with no header -> note X-RateLimit-Remaining
Repeat with header 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7', then '...8'
Observe remaining jumps back to 719 (a fresh bucket) for each spoofed value
expected: The IP-keyed public limiter (issue #88) should throttle a single abusive client regardless of client-supplied headers
actual: ClientIpResolver.resolveClientIp() returns the first X-Forwarded-For hop unconditionally, with no trusted-proxy allow-list. A hostile guest sets a new XFF per request and gets a fresh bucket every time, so the only throttle on fake orders is bypassable. (In prod this depends on the ingress overwriting XFF; the application trusts it blind.)
realWorldImpact: Removes the single brake on KYL-01. With header rotation the 10-order burst becomes an unbounded flood of fake orders against any shop, from one machine.

title: No upper limit on item quantity: a £19 billion order (quantity 2,147,483,647) is accepted and shown on the dashboard
steps: POST a guest order with items:[{productId: <jollof>, quantity: 999}] -> 201, total £8,981.01
POST again with quantity: 2147483647 -> 201, total £19,305,877,986.53
Both appear as PENDING in the vendor Orders list
expected: A sane per-line quantity ceiling (and a basket-total sanity cap) rejecting obvious garbage
actual: Quantity is only validated as >= 1 (negatives, 0 and empty baskets are correctly rejected 400). There is no maximum, so absurd quantities create real orders and real line totals.
realWorldImpact: Pollutes the kitchen queue and the finance ledger with impossible numbers; a vendor glancing at 'Total' sees £8,981 or £19bn against their shop. Confuses takings, breaks any revenue chart, and wastes time working out it is a prank.

title: No bulk-reject and no fraud signal: the vendor must cancel every fake order one at a time, with nothing to tell junk from real
steps: View the vendor Orders page with 15 kyle-p2 fake orders present
Each row has its own Confirm / Cancel button; there is no select-all, no bulk action, no 'suspected spam' flag
expected: A way to triage a wave of suspicious orders: bulk-reject, a risk/new-email flag, or a hold-for-review state
actual: Orders are confirmed/cancelled individually. A throwaway-email order with phone 'x' looks identical to a genuine one. 25 fake orders = 25 manual cancels.
realWorldImpact: Even once the vendor realises they are being trolled, clearing the mess is slow manual work during service. The product gives them no help distinguishing or dispatching the junk.

title: A collection shop accepts a delivery order to an address 300+ miles away for a flat £3.50 fee
steps: POST a DELIVERY order to Mama Ade's (Peckham) with addressPostcode 'EH2 2AN' (Edinburgh), 2x jollof to clear the £10 minimum
-> 201, deliveryFee £3.50, total £21.48, PENDING
expected: A serviceability / radius check rejecting an address the kitchen cannot deliver to
actual: Any valid-format UK postcode is accepted with the flat delivery fee; no distance gate at order time (discovery computes distance but checkout ignores it).
realWorldImpact: A vendor could confirm and plan to fulfil an order that is physically undeliverable, or dispatch a driver on a hopeless trip. Also a griefing vector: order 'delivery' to the far end of the country.

title: Contact details are barely validated: phone 'x', 'no', 'call me', '1' and fake names are all accepted
steps: Place orders with customerPhone values 'call me', 'no', 'x', '0', '1' and junk names
All accepted 201
expected: At least a plausible-phone / plausible-name check on an order the vendor may need to call back about
actual: GuestOrderRequest only length-caps these fields; any non-empty string passes. (Reconfirms pass-1 F-07 for email/phone, extended to clearly fake values.)
realWorldImpact: A no-show prank order gives the vendor no way to chase the customer: the phone is 'x'. Combined with KYL-01 this makes every fake order a dead end.

title: The '20% OFF' promo is advertised on the storefront but never applied to the order total
steps: Shop page shows 'E2E 20% OFF' banner and promotion chip
Place an order; the confirmation total is full price (no discount line, no promo field in the request)
expected: Either the advertised discount is applied, or there is no public discount claim
actual: Promotions are display-only metadata (PublicStorefrontService maps them for config/announcements); OrderService never reads ShopPromotion when pricing. There is no promo-code field to stack or reuse — but the advertised discount is simply never honoured.
realWorldImpact: Not an abuse vector (good: nothing to stack/replay), but a customer who orders expecting 20% off is overcharged versus the banner. A prankster can screenshot the mismatch as a 'false advertising' complaint.

title: No stored XSS: HTML/script in name and notes, RTL-override chars and an emoji flood are stored raw but render as inert text everywhere, and emails are plain text
steps: Order with name '' and notes ' + 60 chilli emoji'
View the vendor Orders and Customers pages with window.alert hooked and dialog listener attached
DOM probe: injected nodes = 0, injected
expected: Payloads must never execute on a vendor screen or in email
actual: React auto-escapes; the JSON-LD serialiser escapes '<'; the order confirmation email is plain text and does not echo the name. Payloads are stored verbatim (seen via vendor API) but are never rendered as markup.
realWorldImpact: A troll cannot hijack a kitchen or admin session through an order note or name. This is a genuine strength and must be preserved.

title: Pricing is server-authoritative: price and total tampered into the request body are ignored
steps: POST an order with items[].pricePennies=1, totalAmountPennies=1, subtotalPennies=1
Server recomputes from the product catalogue: priced at £8.99, then rejected 400 as below the £10 minimum
expected: The client cannot set its own prices
actual: GuestOrderItemRequest only carries productId + quantity; extra fields are ignored and the server prices and enforces the minimum from its own data.
realWorldImpact: A fraudster cannot buy £50 of food for 1p. Strong.

title: Order items are isolated: another shop's product, an unavailable product, and a non-existent product are all rejected 404
steps: Order at Mama Ade's containing Peckham Jollof Co.'s Grilled Tilapia -> 404 Product not found
Order containing an available=false product (Cold Meat Pie) -> 404
Order containing a random UUID -> 404
expected: You can only order this shop's currently-available products
realWorldImpact: No cross-menu order poisoning; no ordering of retired/hidden items.

title: Review abuse is blocked: you cannot review a shop you never ordered from, an order you don't own, a non-completed order, or the same order twice
steps: POST a review with a random orderId -> 404 Order not found
POST a review for an order that is only PENDING -> rejected
Code: review requires email == order.customerEmail, status COMPLETED, and no existing review for that order
expected: Only a customer who actually completed an order can review it, once
actual: Enforced server-side (ReviewService): ownership, COMPLETED status, duplicate guard.
realWorldImpact: No fake 1-star bombing with someone else's order number; no review spam.

title: Order tracking cannot be enumerated and idempotency keys cannot be abused
steps: GET a real order number with a wrong email -> 404; with the right email -> 200
GET /public/orders?email=...&verify= (blank) -> 400, a recent order number is mandatory
Reuse an Idempotency-Key with a DIFFERENT body -> 422 Idempotency Key Reused
expected: Order details need both order number and matching email; no bare-email listing; key reuse is safe
actual: All enforced. Same key + same body replays the original; same key + different body is a 422, not a silent duplicate or overwrite.
realWorldImpact: A troll cannot scrape other customers' orders or smuggle a different order under a replayed key.
